source_type: Normative authority — MET Malaysia operational warning criteria
citation: MET Malaysia (ongoing) — Kawasan Perairan warning bulletin; Category 1 = berbahaya kepada bot-bot kecil (dangerous to small boats).
study_context: Malaysia-wide coastal warning system for marine operators. Category 1 is the entry-level marine advisory indicating elevated risk.
population: All Malaysian marine operators including small vessels.
vessel_context: Small boats (bot-bot kecil) — directly names the deployment population.
environmental_context: Marine warning at Category 1 level — explicitly flagged as hazardous for small vessels.
supported_relationship: When a Category 1 marine advisory is active MET Malaysia explicitly states conditions are dangerous for small boats. This is a direct normative statement about small vessel risk under these conditions.
recommendation_implication: Delay advisory under CAUTION with m = advisory (Category 1). The institution responsible for Malaysian marine safety guidance explicitly identifies Category 1 as hazardous for small vessels — the strongest available justification for a Delay advisory under these conditions.
direct_or_inferred: Direct — the source explicitly states conditions are dangerous for the deployment population.
transferability_to_Sabah: VERY HIGH — this IS the Malaysian normative authority for the study site.
limitations: None relevant to applicability. Category 1 is defined by MET Malaysia for Malaysian waters including Sabah. No geographic adaptation required.

citation: Rahim et al. (2024). Survival Decisions and Adaptation Strategies of Small-scale Fishers in the Face of Extreme Weather Impacts in Coastal Areas. Journal of Marine and Island Cultures v13n3.
study_context: 79 small-scale fishing households, coastal Makassar City, Indonesia. Three distinct seasonal behavioral regimes documented with explicit wind/wave/precipitation characteristics and fisher behavioral responses.
population: Small-scale fishers in coastal Indonesia — similar socioeconomic profile to Malaysian Zone A fishers (low income, small vessels, weather-dependent operations).
vessel_context: Small vessels <10 GRT operating within coastal range. Similar vessel class to Kota Kinabalu Zone A small-scale fishers.
environmental_context: Three seasons: Fishing season (SAFE-equivalent: light wind, moderate rain, mild swells — full operations); East season (CAUTION-equivalent: heavy rain, calm seas, ~5 kn wind — restricted operations); West season (UNSAFE-equivalent: 30-40 kn gusts, >2m waves — full halt).
supported_relationship: SAFE conditions (Fishing season) -> full operations (Go behavioral analog). CAUTION conditions (East season — heavy rainfall with calm seas) -> restricted operations: trips reduced from 5-6/week to 2-3/week, duration reduced from 7-10 hours to 3-5 hours, near-shore only (Delay behavioral analog). UNSAFE conditions (West season) -> complete halt (AI off).
recommendation_implication: Go advisory in SAFE state (behavioral basis: fishers go out under Fishing season conditions). Delay advisory in CAUTION state driven by heavy rainfall (behavioral basis: Rahim East season restricted operations — the most direct empirical evidence for rainfall-driven Delay).
direct_or_inferred: Inferred from documented fisher behavioral patterns. Not a direct advisory rule specification — behavioral restriction under CAUTION-equivalent conditions is taken as the empirical basis for Delay.
transferability_to_Sabah: MODERATE — Indonesian coastal fishers have comparable socioeconomic profile and small-vessel operations but Indonesian coastal waters differ from Sabah's coastal environment. Wind regimes and seasonality differ. Adaptation to Sabah conditions required.
limitations: Key limitation: East season conditions appear internally contradictory (vigorous winds / 5 kn wind). Source-verified 2026-09-06: contradiction is in the source; heavy rainfall is confirmed as the driver of restricted operations, not wind. Indonesian context limits direct transferability. n=79 in a single location.

source_type: Domain empirical study — qualitative fisher decision mapping
citation: Gao (2024). Mapping the Decision-Making Factors of Small-Scale Fishers: A Case Study of Penang. M.Sc. thesis, IMRD/WorldFish, University of Pisa.
study_context: 25 semi-structured interviews with small-scale gill net fishers in Penang, Malaysia. Three-tier decision structure empirically documented.
population: Penang Zone A small-scale fishers — same national context (Malaysia) and zone designation as Kota Kinabalu. Gill net operators, 1-3 person boats, within 5nm of shore.
vessel_context: Small vessels <40 GRT, Zone A (0-5nm). Gill nets, 1-3 crew. Closest available study population to Kota Kinabalu Zone A.
environmental_context: Tripartite informal classification: go (favourable) / cautious-go (marginal) / don't go (adverse). Go conditions: fishers make full operational decisions. Cautious-go conditions: near-shore only, heightened monitoring, shortened trips. Weather importance rating 3.75/5.
supported_relationship: SAFE conditions (full decision scope) -> Go behavioral analog. Marginal conditions (cautious-go) -> restricted operations (Delay behavioral analog). Adverse conditions (if wind too strong don't go) -> halt (AI off). Direct fisher quote: If the wind is too strong I don't go.
recommendation_implication: Go advisory in SAFE state (tripartite behavioral structure with Go equivalent). Delay advisory in CAUTION state — cautious-go restricted operations including shortened trips and near-shore constraint maps to Delay.
direct_or_inferred: Inferred from documented behavioral patterns and fisher decision mapping. Not a direct rule specification. Provides behavioral analog for Go/Delay in respective states.
transferability_to_Sabah: HIGH — Malaysian context (Penang). Zone A small-scale fishers with same regulatory framework. Same vessel class and proximity constraints. Geographic adaptation from Penang to Sabah coastal waters is smaller than for international studies but still required. Penang fisher practices may differ from Sabah indigenous coastal fishers.
limitations: Unpublished M.Sc. thesis — not peer-reviewed. Small sample n=25. Qualitative methodology with potential recall bias. Tide was highest-rated factor (4.55) and is absent from E vector — a documented limitation. Geographic distance Penang to Sabah.

source_type: Empirical peer-reviewed study — hazard perception and behavioral evidence
citation: Yamin et al. (2025). Interplay of traditional knowledge and adaptive capacity in climate change adaptation of small-scale fishers in central Terengganu, Malaysia. Frontiers in Marine Science, 12:1492131.
study_context: 136 small-scale fishers across five coastal villages in central Terengganu (Q1 journal, primary empirical data). SEM analysis.
population: Terengganu small-scale fishers — Zone A (0-5nm), traditional vessels <40 GRT, 95% report stronger winds and waves as primary hazard, 91% report erratic rainfall as primary hazard.
vessel_context: Zone A small-scale fishers. Hook-and-line (most common), gillnet, bubu. 40.4% fish alone; 52.9% require 2-6 crew. Trip duration approximately 1 day.
environmental_context: Wind and waves (95% agreement as primary hazard), rainfall (91%), monsoon unpredictability. Empirical knowledge item: If it is suddenly windy/change of weather I can't go fishing.
supported_relationship: Sudden weather change -> cannot go fishing (binary Go/No-Go confirmed). Flexibility is the weakest adaptive capacity domain (only 58% willing to consider alternatives) — Delay behavioral pattern is currently absent from fisher repertoire and represents the graduated response the CAUTION mode enables.
recommendation_implication: Corroborates Go/no-go structure in SAFE/UNSAFE states. Establishes that the Delay advisory represents a genuinely novel graduated response not currently in fisher behavioral repertoire — strengthens the architecture's contribution.
direct_or_inferred: Inferred — the study documents the binary go/no-go pattern and establishes that Delay represents a capability gap rather than replication of existing behavior.
transferability_to_Sabah: HIGH — Malaysian context (Terengganu). Very close socioeconomic and regulatory profile to Kota Kinabalu Zone A fishers. Adaptation from East Coast to West Coast (Sabah) waters required.
limitations: Q1 journal but dataset is perception-based (fisher self-report on hazard frequency). No direct departure-time or trip-duration data. Terengganu faces northeast monsoon more severely than Sabah. n=136 but from one coastal region.

source_type: Empirical peer-reviewed study — departure restriction for small fishing vessels by wave height
citation: Jeong & Im (2023). Proposal of Restrictions on the Departure of Korea Small Fishing Vessel according to Wave Height. Journal of Marine Science and Engineering 11:1302.
study_context: 66 small fishing vessel capsizing incidents in Korean coastal waters (1999-2022). Analysis of vessel-length-dependent departure restriction thresholds using Wolfson Unit formula.
population: Korean small fishing vessels <10 tons — 89% of accidents involve <10-ton vessels. LOA range 10-24m.
vessel_context: Small fishing vessels; length-dependent thresholds: Hs_KIMO approx 1.13m (LOA 10m) to 2.07m (LOA 24m). Proposed management: caution at Hs >= 1.0m for vessels <=10m.
environmental_context: Wave height as the primary departure restriction variable. 38% of all capsizing incidents occurred at Hs <= 3m. Capsizing documented at Hs as low as 1.0m.
supported_relationship: Small vessels <10m LOA: departure caution should begin at Hs >= 1.0m (Hs_KIMO approx 1.13m for 10m vessel). Graduated restriction framework proposed (three tiers).
recommendation_implication: Wave height in CAUTION range for vessel category -> Delay advisory. Provides the departure-restriction evidence that justifies wave-conditioned Delay recommendation within CAUTION state.
direct_or_inferred: Inferred from departure restriction framework. Departure restriction (binary halt) is stronger than Delay advisory — the implication is that if departure restriction begins at 1.0m then Delay advisory is warranted at these wave heights.
transferability_to_Sabah: MODERATE — Korean vessel geometry (beam-to-length ratios) may differ from traditional Malaysian wooden fishing vessels. Formula calibrated to Korean vessel specifications. Geographic and vessel-type adaptation required. The 1.0m threshold from the management proposal aligns with the architecture's small-vessel CAUTION onset.
limitations: Korean vessels, not Malaysian. Formula based on UK Wolfson Unit MCA research adapted to Korean proportions — not validated for Malaysian traditional fishing vessels. Capsizing analysis does not establish advisory content beyond binary restriction.

source_type: Empirical peer-reviewed study — Malaysian vessel seakeeping and operability limits
citation: Yaakob et al. (2015). Stability, Seakeeping and Safety Assessment of Small Fishing Boats Operating in Southern Coast of Peninsular Malaysia. Journal of Sustainability Science and Management 10(1):50-65.
study_context: Two traditional Malaysian small fishing boats from Johor coast (Mersing and Pontian). Naval architecture assessment using Maxsurf/Hydromax/Seakeeper. NORDFORSK 1987 and IMO stability criteria.
population: Malaysian Zone A small fishing boats <10 GRT: Boat A (6.54m LOA, 1.48m breadth) and Boat B (5.03m LOA, 1.32m breadth). Wooden construction, outboard motors, no radar.
vessel_context: Both boats <10 GRT, Zone A (<10nm from shore). Traditional Malaysian wooden hull construction. Directly from the deployment population country (Malaysia). Johor coast (South China Sea and Straits of Malacca).
environmental_context: Wave height operability: Boat A fails NORDFORSK at SS4 (Hs approx 1.875m). Boat A operational limit: SS3 (Hs up to ~1.25m). Boat B fails NORDFORSK at SS3 (Hs approx 0.875m). Boat B operational limit: SS2 (Hs up to ~0.5m).
supported_relationship: Malaysian small fishing vessels (6.54m LOA) exceed seakeeping operability criteria at Hs approx 1.875m. Operational limit approximately 1.25m for larger small vessels. Static stability passes across all conditions — dynamic seakeeping is the limiting factor.
recommendation_implication: Wave height approaching or within CAUTION range for small vessels warrants operational concern. Provides hydrodynamic evidence for vessel-specific wave height thresholds in Malaysian context.
direct_or_inferred: Inferred from seakeeping operability analysis. NORDFORSK failure means crew cannot safely perform heavy manual work — implies departure restriction rather than departure advisory. Translation to Delay advisory requires interpretation.
transferability_to_Sabah: MODERATE-HIGH — Only peer-reviewed study of actual Malaysian small fishing vessels using naval architecture methods. Geographic limitation: Johor (southern coast, South China Sea and Straits of Malacca) rather than Sabah (Sulu Sea and South China Sea, northwest Borneo). Two-vessel sample is very limited. Different hull geometries and sea states from Sabah waters.
limitations: n=2 boats. Only small-vessel category covered — no medium or big vessel data. Johor coast wave conditions differ from Sabah coastal waters. NORDFORSK heavy manual work criterion is a proxy for operability, not a departure restriction criterion. Traditional fishing vessel design may have changed since 2015 though generally stable.

source_type: Empirical peer-reviewed study — risk perception in small-scale fishing navigation
citation: Atacan & Duzbastilar (2023). Determination of risk perception in small-scale fishing and navigation. Ege Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 40(1):1-14.
study_context: 30 small-scale fishing vessel captains from two Turkish fishing ports (n=20 Iskele, n=10 Cesmealtı). Bridge navigation simulator under six environmental scenarios. Fine-Kinney risk assessment.
population: Active Turkish small-scale fishing vessel captains (LOA ~18m in simulator). Mediterranean context.
vessel_context: Small-scale fishing vessels LOA ~18m in simulator (upper end of small-scale). All participants from same vessel type and class.
environmental_context: Six environmental conditions tested: calm weather/sea, current (4 knots), restricted visibility (100m), night navigation, heavy weather (5 Beaufort), night + heavy weather. Night navigation significantly increases accident probability (mean 4.08 vs 3.43 calm) and consequence (mean 12.80 vs 8.53 calm). Heavy weather alone: probability 4.48, consequence 24.83. Combined night + heavy weather: probability 5.56 (port), consequence 37.03 (sea).
supported_relationship: Night navigation substantially elevates accident probability and consequence severity for small-scale fishing vessel captains. Heavy weather (5 Beaufort approx 17-21 kn sustained wind) also significantly elevates risk. Combined conditions produce highest risk scores. Authors recommend cancellation if precautions cannot reduce probability.
recommendation_implication: Empirical support for g_t (nighttime -> UNSAFE) classification. Secondary support for wind-driven risk at CAUTION levels (5 Beaufort approaching Layer 2 CAUTION threshold). Fisher risk perception aligns with Layer 2 classification logic.
direct_or_inferred: Inferred from risk perception data and pro-active departure assessment framing. Establishes that fishers themselves perceive elevated risk under the conditions the architecture classifies as CAUTION/UNSAFE.
transferability_to_Sabah: LOW — Turkish Mediterranean context substantially different from Malaysian Sabah coastal fishers. Different vessel types (simulated 18m LOA vs typical 5-7m Sabah Zone A boats). Different meteorological and oceanographic regimes. Primarily supports Layer 2 (g_t and g_w classification) rather than Layer 3 advisory content.
limitations: Turkish Mediterranean context limits transferability. Simulator fidelity may not match real conditions. Small sample n=30. Risk perception does not translate directly to advisory content.

source_type: Internal synthesis document — label derivation combining three empirical studies (EV-02, EV-03, EV-04). Not an independent empirical source.
citation: dataset-label-derivation.md — internal project document (May 2026; SDR-001 updated 2026-09-08) synthesizing training labels from Rahim et al. (2024) [EV-02], Gao (2024) [EV-03], and Yamin et al. (2025) [EV-04].
study_context: Label derivation methodology for the advisory AI training dataset. Synthesizes three independent empirical studies into a Go/Delay label mapping. Purpose is ML training label specification, not independent empirical research.
population: Not an original study — documents the synthesis of three studies: Indonesia (n=79 from EV-02), Penang (n=25 from EV-03), Terengganu (n=136 from EV-04). Cross-validated behavioral patterns from the three underlying sources.
vessel_context: Small vessels <10 GRT (small vessel category primary deployment population), as documented in the three underlying studies.
environmental_context: Vessel-conditional wave thresholds applied. Conditions mapped to MET Malaysia Kawasan Perairan range bands. Environmental context inherited from EV-02, EV-03, EV-04.
supported_relationship: Synthesized label logic: SAFE conditions -> Go label; CAUTION conditions (four antecedents: wind CAUTION band, wave CAUTION band, heavy rain, Category 1 warning) -> Delay label; UNSAFE conditions -> AI advisory unavailable. This synthesis is consistent with the three underlying studies but does not add independent empirical content.
recommendation_implication: Go advisory in SAFE state (all-SAFE conditions). Delay advisory in CAUTION state across four antecedent types. DepartureTime and Duration deferred to RQ5. All advisory implications derive from EV-02, EV-03, or EV-04.
direct_or_inferred: Internal synthesis — label logic derived by combining EV-02 (Rahim 2024), EV-03 (Gao 2024), and EV-04 (Yamin 2025). Not independently evidenced. Any claim attributable solely to EV-08 reduces to claims from the three underlying studies. Should not be counted as a fourth independent empirical source.
transferability_to_Sabah: MODERATE — same geographic limitations as the three underlying studies (Indonesia/Penang/Terengganu -> Sabah). Document purpose is ML training label derivation; adaptation to rule-based Layer 3 requires external validation.
limitations: Internal document — not externally peer-reviewed. Label derivation involves interpretation of qualitative behavioral studies. Studies are from different geographic regions. EV-08 synthesizes EV-02, EV-03, and EV-04: it is not a fourth independent empirical source. Any claim attributable solely to EV-08 reduces to claims from the underlying studies.

source_type: Canonical formalisation — formal semantic definitions of recommendation types
citation: appendix-c-formalisation.md — canonical formalisation document; Section C.4 defines R = {Go, Delay, DepartureTime, Duration} with brief definitions.
study_context: Canonical formalisation of the architecture's formal model.
population: Not applicable — formal document not empirical study.
recommendation_implication: Formal definitions: Go = go/no-go recommendation; Delay = recommendation to delay departure; DepartureTime = recommended departure window; Duration = recommended safe trip duration. These are definitional constraints on the semantic meaning of each type.
direct_or_inferred: Constrains the semantic interpretation of each recommendation type. The Go definition confirms Go does not mean permission. The Delay definition confirms Delay means defer departure. Neither definition establishes empirically justified antecedent conditions.
transferability_to_Sabah: HIGH — canonical document for this project. Not geographically limited.
limitations: Definitional only — specifies what each type means, not when to recommend it. Does not establish empirically justified antecedent conditions.
